newsitem.title: USA: NYSE Dec 30-Jan 3 program trading average 15.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: NYSE Dec 30-Jan 3 program trading average 15.4 pct.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said program trading averaged 15.4 percent of its average daily volume of 413.3 million shares, or 63.8 million shares, for the week of December 30, 1996 to January 3, 1997.
Of the average 63.8 million shares during the week, buy programs accounted for an average 28.5 million shares, while sell programs accounted for an average 35.3 million daily.
In all markets, program trading averaged 93.3 million shares a day during the week of December 30 to January 3.

Of the five member firms reporting the most program activity on the New York Stock Exchange, BNP Securities, Salomon Brothers and Susquehanna Brokerage Services conducted most or all of their program activity for customers, as agent or facilitator. Morgan Stanley and Lehman Brothers executed most of their program activity as principal, for their own accounts.

Program trading executed by firms as agent, for non-member customers, amounted to 70.3 percent during the week, while volume executed as principal, for their own accounts, amounted to 28.7 percent of program volume from December 30 to January 3.

Between December 30 and January 3, 20.4 percent of program trading volume executed by NYSE member firms was related to index arbitrage, while another 1.4 percent involved other derivative product-related strategies.
Program trading encompasses trading strategies involving the sale or purchase of a basket of at least 15 stocks with a value of $1 million or more the exchange said.
